assumptions.condition: The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with law induced by \(P\).

standard.name: No anticipation through the last pre-treatment date

assumptions.condition: \(Z\) has exactly the two support points \(1\) and \(2\).
Conditional on \((D,Z)\), each marginal potential path \((X_0(r),\ldots,X_4(r))\) is first-order Markov.
For each potential path, \(P(X_{t+1}(r)=e\mid X_t(r)=e,D,Z)=1\) whenever \(t<4\).

novel.justification: This observable support-face restriction describes cohorts formed before any recorded exit, as with incumbent firms, enrolled students, or initially unemployed workers whose first analyzed spell begins while active.

standard.name: Type-specific transition independence at date two
Type-specific transition independence at the first post-treatment date
Type-specific transition independence at date four
Matched-slice nonsingularity on an active minor
Compact separation from singular recovery boundaries
Positive marginal-variance condition allowing singular correlation

definitions.name: Compatible full-data fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F(p)=\{\widetilde P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}:\widetilde P(O=s)=p_s\text{ for every observed cell }s\}\).

definitions.name: Observed matched slices and cycle product
definitions.construction: For each \(d\) and \(x,y\in\mathcal A\), tabulate \(A_{xy}^d[u,v]=P(X_0=u,X_1=x,X_2=y,X_3=v\mid D=d)\), retain \(\bar A_{xy}^d=A_{xy}^d[:,\mathcal A]\), tabulate \(m_x^d[u]=P(X_0=u,X_1=x\mid D=d)\), and set \(K^d=\bar A_{aa}^d(\bar A_{ba}^d)^{-1}\bar A_{bb}^d(\bar A_{ab}^d)^{-1}\).

definitions.name: Projector-and-row-sum recovery map
definitions.construction: For each cohort \(d\), calculate \(g^d\), \(\rho_j^d\), \(P_j^d\), \(B_a^d=[P_1^dm_a^d,P_2^dm_a^d]\), \(F_y^d=(B_a^d)^{-1}A_{ay}^d\), \(q_{ay}^d=F_y^d\mathbf 1_3\), \(C_y^d=\operatorname{diag}(q_{ay}^d)^{-1}F_y^d\), \(W^d=A_{ba}^d(C_a^d)^\top\{C_a^d(C_a^d)^\top\}^{-1}\), \(c^d=(W^d)^{-1}m_b^d\), and \(B_b^d=W^d\operatorname{diag}(c^d)\). Fill \(\widehat Q_j^d\) from \(q_{ay}^d\), \((B_b^d)^{-1}A_{by}^d\mathbf 1_3\), stochastic exit residuals, and the absorbing row; fill \(\widehat R_j^d\) from the rows of \(C_y^d\) and the absorbing row. Set \(\widehat\pi_j^d=\sum_u(B_a^d[u,j]+B_b^d[u,j])\), \(\widehat p_{2,j}^d=(\widehat\pi_j^d)^{-1}(\sum_uB_a^d[u,j],\sum_uB_b^d[u,j],0)\widehat Q_j^d\), and order by \(\rho_1^d>\rho_2^d\). Finally, \(\Phi(p)=((\widehat p_{2,1}^1(\widehat R_1^1-\widehat R_1^0))^\top,(\widehat p_{2,2}^1(\widehat R_2^1-\widehat R_2^0))^\top,(\sum_j\widehat\pi_j^1\widehat p_{2,j}^1(\widehat R_j^1-\widehat R_j^0))^\top)^\top\).

definitions.name: Complete observable recovery-margin vector
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak m(p)\) lists both cohort shares, all recovered type shares, \(g^d\), the smallest singular values of every \(\bar A_{xy}^d\), \(B_a^d\), \(B_b^d\), \(W^d\), and \(C_y^d(C_y^d)^\top\), the absolute values of every entry of \(q_{ay}^d\), \(q_{by}^d\), \(c^d\), and \(\widehat\pi_j^d\) used in a division, and the distance between the two common untreated signatures whose first coordinates are \(\rho_1^d\) and \(\rho_2^d\).

definitions.name: Compact buffered recovery class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}=\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}:\min_k\mathfrak m_k(p)\geq2\kappa\text{ and }\min_{\ell\in\mathcal L}\Sigma_{\ell\ell}(p)\geq2\kappa\}\), with closure taken inside the finite-parameter compatible image.

definitions.name: Guarded empirical-cell plug-in
definitions.construction: Evaluate the entries of \(\mathfrak m(\widehat p)\) sequentially, stopping before an inverse or division whose required margin is at most \(\kappa\); also require legal support and \(\widehat\Sigma_{\ell\ell}>\kappa\) for every \(\ell\in\mathcal L\). This event is \(\mathcal E_{\kappa}\). On \(\mathcal E_{\kappa}\), set \(\widehat\theta=\Phi(\widehat p)\), \(\widehat G_i=J_{\Phi}(\widehat p)(e_{O_i}-\widehat p)\), and \(\widehat\Sigma=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat G_i\widehat G_i^\top\); otherwise report that the sample is outside the regular recovery domain and return no interval.

definitions.name: Gaussian-multiplier simultaneous band
definitions.construction: Conditionally on the sample, draw \(\xi_i\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(0,1)\), form \(T^\star=\max_{\ell\in\mathcal L}|n^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i\widehat G_{i,\ell}|/\sqrt{\widehat\Sigma_{\ell\ell}}\), take its exact conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile \(\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\), and report \(I_{\ell,n}=[\widehat\theta_\ell\mathbin{-}\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{\widehat\Sigma_{\ell\ell}/n},\widehat\theta_\ell\mathbin{+}\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{\widehat\Sigma_{\ell\ell}/n}]\).

definitions.name: Exact rational absorbing-face witness
definitions.construction: Let \(P(D=1)=1/2\), \(\pi_1^d=\pi_2^d=1/2\), and let \(X_0\) be uniform on \(\mathcal A\) conditional on \((Z,D)\). With row and column order \((a,b,e)\), set \(H_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}3/4&1/4&0\\1/4&3/4&0\\0&0&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(H_2=\begin{psmallmatrix}1/3&2/3&0\\2/3&1/3&0\\0&0&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(Q_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}3/5&3/10&1/10\\1/5&1/2&3/10\\0&0&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(Q_2=\begin{psmallmatrix}1/5&2/5&2/5\\3/10&3/5&1/10\\0&0&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(V_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}7/10&1/5&1/10\\1/5&3/5&1/5\\0&0&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), and \(V_2=\begin{psmallmatrix}1/5&1/2&3/10\\1/4&1/2&1/4\\0&0&1\end{psmallmatrix}\). Use \(H_j\) from date \(0\) to \(1\), \(Q_j\) for untreated transitions from dates \(1\) to \(2\) and \(2\) to \(3\), and \(V_j\) for the treated transition from date \(2\) to \(3\); extend through date \(4\) by the same relevant kernel. This law is \(\omega^\star\).

definitions.name: Initial-absorption observational-equivalence pair
definitions.construction: Mix \(4/5\) of \(\omega^\star\) with an all-exit path of probability \(1/5\) in each cohort. In \(P^A\), allocate all added mass to type \(1\); in \(P^B\), allocate it to type \(2\), leaving every type-specific transition kernel fixed.

definitions.name: Constrained Markov efficiency handle
definitions.construction: Differentiate the polynomial equalities encoding absorption, the two-type Markov factorization, common untreated kernels, and the fifth-date restrictions to characterize \(\mathcal T_P\); project the saturated gradient \(G_p\) onto that score space and use the resulting normal equations as the starting point for constructing a regular estimator of \(\theta\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\), the recovery map is well-defined and \(\Phi(p)=\theta\). More strongly, for every \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal F(p)\), the formulas recover the same \(\pi_j^d\), the same component law of \((Z,X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3)\) in each cohort, and the same \(\tau_j\) and \(\tau\), up to the declared descending \(\rho_j^d\) order. The result holds without time homogeneity and on laws with the common absorbing row that violate the all-state terminal-rank and positive-transition conditions used by the adjacent recovery theorems.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it converts four observable active minors and stochastic normalization into latent path and ATT recovery on a structurally singular support face.
statements.gap: Ahn and Kasahara, Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, and Higgins and Jochmans, Theorem 1, recover latent Markov laws through full-rank spectral factorizations, but their stated conditions do not cover a state that is absorbing for every type; the present claim proves fiberwise recovery on that excluded face.
statements.consumer: Rao and Risch's incumbent-firm panel can use low- and high-productivity active states plus exit to distinguish offsetting type-specific exit responses hidden by a nearly flat aggregate exit effect.

statements.statement: The exact law \(\omega^\star\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\), has \(K^0=K^1=\begin{psmallmatrix}29/5&-12/5\\8/5&1/5\end{psmallmatrix}\) with ordered spectrum \((5,1)\), and satisfies \(\tau_1=(1/25,0,-1/25)\), \(\tau_2=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20)\), and \(\tau=(3/400,-1/80,1/200)\). By contrast, \(P^A\) and \(P^B\) induce the same observed five-date law, active slices, and cycle product while their type shares are \((3/5,2/5)\) and \((2/5,3/5)\), respectively, and their type-specific exit ATT pairs are \((-2/75,1/20)\) and \((-1/25,1/30)\). Hence deleting \(\text{ass:no-date-one-absorption}\) destroys identification of type masses and conditional type effects, although this pair leaves the aggregate exit ATT equal to \(1/250\).
statements.justification: The witness establishes nonvacuity, checks every normalization exactly, and identifies the precise role of the initial support face for the conditional targets.
statements.gap: Existing absorbing-outcome DiD results do not provide a two-type multi-state observational-equivalence calculation, and generic mixture results do not isolate the initial-absorber allocation that breaks conditional ATT recovery.
statements.consumer: Applied researchers can treat baseline exit as a falsifiable support diagnostic and avoid interpreting conditional latent-type effects when baseline absorbers are present.

statements.statement: The map \(\Phi\) extends real analytically to an open neighborhood of every regular \(p\) satisfying the identification assumptions. In the saturated finite-multinomial model on the declared support stratum, \(G_p(s)=J_{\Phi}(p)(e_s-p)\) is the canonical gradient of \(\Phi(p)\), \(\Sigma(p)\) is its information bound, and the empirical-cell plug-in attains this bound at every relative-interior law on that stratum.
statements.justification: Analyticity makes the influence function explicit and turns a constructive identification formula into a regular finite-multinomial estimator.
statements.gap: Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin differentiate simultaneous-diagonalization estimators for nonexchangeable latent models, while Ahn and Kasahara use interior likelihood asymptotics; neither gives the canonical gradient of this row-sum and pseudoinverse map on an absorbing support stratum.
statements.consumer: Implementers obtain a closed-form delta-method variance that includes estimated type masses and avoids repeated nonconvex likelihood optimization.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}\), \(P(\mathcal E_{\kappa})\to1\), \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta-\theta\}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nG_p(O_i)+o_P(1)\), and \(\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma(p)=o_P(1)\). Moreover, allowing \(\Sigma(p)\) to be singular while retaining its buffered reported diagonal, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}}P(\theta_\ell\in I_{\ell,n}\text{ for every }\ell\in\mathcal L)\to1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: The coverage theorem integrates data-dependent numerical guards with a singular-correlation Gaussian maximum, the unresolved proof boundary left by pointwise interior theory.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato allow arbitrary Gaussian correlation under positive marginal variances, but do not study a guarded rational spectral map; Ahn and Kasahara's weighted-bootstrap intervals do not establish uniform acceptance and coverage on an absorbing face.
statements.consumer: Users can report joint bands for all type-specific and aggregate state effects even when adding-up identities make the nine-dimensional covariance singular.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{eff}}\), characterize the efficient influence function and efficiency bound for \(\theta\) in the constrained model \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\) that exploits common untreated kernels, the latent Markov factorization, and date \(4\); determine whether a regular estimator attains that bound uniformly on \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}\), and characterize exactly when its variance is strictly below \(\Sigma(p)\).
statements.justification: The saturated gradient deliberately leaves information in the common-kernel restrictions and fifth date unused, so the constrained efficiency problem is genuine rather than a routine restatement.
statements.gap: Newey supplies the tangent-space projection principle and Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin derive regular spectral-estimator asymptotics, but no adjacent paper characterizes the tangent space or efficient ATT score for this absorbing latent Markov face.
statements.consumer: A solution would tell practitioners whether the transparent four-slice estimator pays an avoidable precision cost and would provide the benchmark for efficient likelihood or minimum-distance implementations.

sampling_model.design: Observational two-cohort panel with adoption at date \(3\) for \(D=1\) and no adoption for \(D=0\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent and identically distributed complete five-date panels \(O_i\).
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort membership fixes the realized treatment path; no anticipation holds through date \(2\).
sampling_model.overlap: Both cohorts have positive probability and both latent types have positive mass within each cohort.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is fitted; empirical frequencies on the fixed \(120\)-cell support face feed the guarded analytic recovery map.

estimand_functional: \(\theta=\Phi(p)=((\widehat p_{2,1}^1(\widehat R_1^1-\widehat R_1^0))^\top,(\widehat p_{2,2}^1(\widehat R_2^1-\widehat R_2^0))^\top,(\sum_{j=1}^2\widehat\pi_j^1\widehat p_{2,j}^1(\widehat R_j^1-\widehat R_j^0))^\top)^\top\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 14 uniquely identifies the finite latent-type Markov parameter under Assumptions RSM, M, and ID from a sufficiently long short panel.
Theorem 1 identifies initial distributions, transition kernels, and type probabilities up to a common permutation from four consecutive observations under Assumptions 1--3.
The paper estimates latent conditional moments by simultaneous diagonalization followed by weighted empirical averages and derives regular asymptotics for the estimated weights.
Gaussian comparison and anti-concentration bounds hold for maxima with arbitrary covariance matrices when marginal variances are positive.
The efficient influence function is obtained by projecting a pathwise derivative onto the model tangent space.

tldr: Four matched active-state slices identify two latent Markov components even when a common absorbing state makes the usual all-state terminal factor singular. Spectral projectors remove eigenvector scaling, full terminal row sums recover exit probabilities, a pseudoinverse transports the second active predecessor factor, and the observable absence of date-‑\(1\) exit exhausts each type mass. The resulting analytic cell-probability map identifies type-specific and aggregate first-post state ATTs over the full compatible fiber, yields a saturated finite-multinomial canonical gradient, and supports guarded Gaussian-multiplier bands uniformly over a compact margin class despite singular ATT correlation. An exact rational witness verifies the map, an outside-face pair shows why initial absorbers break conditional type recovery, and constrained-Markov efficiency remains the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Short-panel latent Markov reconstruction uses nonsingular terminal factors and positive transition arrays, while causal transition-independence work inherits those conditions; a common absorbing observed state creates identical terminal rows and structural zeros, and existing pointwise likelihood inference does not cover a data-dependent guarded recovery map on that face.
project_justification.niche: Two active states and one absorbing exit state still leave four invertible active minors whose cycle product carries type signatures, while stochastic row sums and no initial absorption contain normalization information absent from a survival-conditioned reduction.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an explicit projector, row-sum, and pseudoinverse recovery formula with a full-fiber uniqueness theorem, exact boundary evidence, an analytic saturated-model gradient, and uniform multiplier coverage under observable buffered margins.

related_work: Ahn and Kasahara (2026), Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, provide the closest causal setup and four-slice inverse-cancellation argument, but Assumption ID requires nonsingular terminal factors and strictly positive transitions that exclude a common absorbing row; their writing arc from incoherent categorical trends to transition-based counterfactuals is retained here. Higgins and Jochmans (2023), Theorem 1 and Sections 2--3, establish constructive Markov-mixture recovery and common label alignment; their full-rank factor logic informs the proof, while the present target uses active minors and stochastic row sums on an excluded support face and is not claimed to subsume their theorem. Gupta, Kumar, and Vassilvitskii (2016) reconstruct homogeneous Markov mixtures under a state-count restriction that does not cover two types with only two active states. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2017) supply the closest estimator template: differentiate a simultaneous-diagonalization construction and propagate estimated weights into conditional moments. Deaner and Ku (2026) show why absorption calls for transition or hazard restrictions, but address binary aggregate duration effects rather than multi-state latent-type recovery. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, 2015) provide multiplier and anti-concentration tools under arbitrary correlation; the new task is their integration with guard-uniform linearization of the spectral map. Newey (1990) supplies the projection geometry for the open constrained-efficiency question. Rao and Risch (2026) are the interpretation consumer because their linked firm panel separates entry and exit adjustments and could distinguish offsetting exit effects across latent productivity types.
technical_internal_limitation: The covariance \(\Sigma(p)\) is the efficiency bound only for the specified off-model continuation \(\Phi\) in the saturated multinomial support-stratum model. It is not asserted to be efficient in the smaller compatible Markov model, which can use common kernels and date \(4\). The initial-absorption pair proves failure of type-mass and conditional-type-effect identification, not failure of aggregate ATT identification. The exact multiplier quantile is the mathematical object; a fixed finite number of Monte Carlo draws requires an additional approximation analysis.
honest_scope: The proposal proves sufficient recovery on a declared regular absorbing face, not a necessary-and-sufficient identification frontier. In the special case of no exit transitions, all exit ATT coordinates reduce to zero and the active-state formulas collapse to ordinary two-state latent Markov recovery; with one latent type, the projector step disappears and the ATT reduces to the transition-independence plug-in. The unresolved content is constrained-model efficiency, while weak eigengaps, unknown type count, initial-absorption sharp bounds, and approximate common transitions remain separate angles.

seed_details.title: Absorbing-face full-fiber recovery

seed_details.opportunity: Replace the anchor's invertible all-state terminal factors by four active minors, projector normalization, full terminal row sums, and a support-face mass equation.

seed_details.opportunity: Test one versus two absorbing Markov types and invert the test for aggregate ATT confidence sets with oracle width away from the boundary.

seed_details.red_team: Kasahara--Shimotsu's modified EM test transfers directly to multinomial panels.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their normal-mixture score expansion does not transfer across structural-zero constraints or propagate component selection into uniform causal-ATT coverage.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A selection-consistent estimator alone is insufficient; the kernel requires uniform confidence sets and a separation scale.

seed_details.title: Unlabeled ATT law at spectral collision
seed_details.anchor_location: Assumption ID(a)(ii) distinct eigenvalues and Appendix A.4 eigenvector recovery; Introduction motivation for latent-type effects and final applications were read.
seed_details.opportunity: Identify or refute identification of the mixing measure \(\sum_j\pi_j^1\delta_{\tau_j}\) at repeated cycle-product eigenvalues.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct basis-invariant moments of the ATT measure from matched slices without individual spectral projectors.
seed_details.red_team: Discarding labels automatically resolves spectral collision.
seed_details.rebuttal: ATT vectors compose projectors with row sums, pseudoinverses, and cohort-specific transitions, so invariance of the quotient law is not automatic and may fail observationally.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The target is the unlabeled mixing law with an identification or impossibility frontier, not arbitrarily relabeled type coefficients.

novelty_justification: The theorem-level delta is not spectral cancellation itself. It is recovery on a support face excluded by the closest all-state rank and positivity conditions: active spectral projectors are scaled by predecessor masses, full terminal row sums restore exit probabilities, a full-row-rank pseudoinverse transports the second predecessor factor, and absence of date-1 absorption exhausts each type mass. The inference delta is uniform guard acceptance and multiplier coverage for this analytic map under singular ATT correlation. The exact witness and outside-face observational-equivalence pair certify nonvacuity and the boundary of conditional type-effect recovery.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic: Four-slice ATT recovery on an absorbing Markov face. Observe iid five-date panels on states {a,b,e}, e absorbing, with treatment adoption at date 3, two known latent types, type-conditional first-order Markov potential paths, no anticipation, cohort/type overlap, and common type-specific untreated transitions. On the declared face with no date-1 absorption, four nonsingular matched active-state slices, simple cycle-product spectrum, nonzero stochastic normalizations, separated common untreated cross-ratios, and buffered variance margins, prove that spectral projectors and row-sum normalization recover type masses, the component path law through date 3, and type-specific plus aggregate first-post state ATTs over the full compatible fiber. Derive guarded empirical-cell plug-in, the saturated finite-multinomial canonical gradient, and uniform Gaussian-multiplier bands. Use the exact H1,H2,Q1,Q2,V1,V2 witness with K=[[29/5,-12/5],[8/5,1/5]], type exit ATTs (-1/25,1/20), aggregate 1/200, and the initial-absorption counterexample. Distinguish Ahn–Kasahara, Markov-mixture reconstruction, Deaner–Ku, and restricted-HMM results; Rao–Risch is the interpretation consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Four matched slices yield K=B_a diag(rho_1,rho_2) B_a^-1; projector normalization B_a=[P_1m_a,P_2m_a], terminal row sums, full-row-rank pseudoinverses, and the no-initial-absorption condition then recover all promised factors. Exact enumeration reproduces state-vector ATTs (1/25,0,-1/25) and (-1/40,-1/40,1/20), aggregate (3/400,-1/80,1/200), while an outside-face construction preserves active slices but changes type effects. Differential recurrences and compact-margin Taylor bounds were derived, with numerical derivatives agreeing to relative error 3.7e-10. Checks covered scaling, equal weights, time variation, pseudoinverses, mass normalization, cohort labels, singular boundaries, support deletion, and neighboring literature; no collision or identification failure survived. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Verify Gaussian-max quantile continuity uniformly over the compact margin class, including singular correlation limits, and combine it with the buffered empirical guard; standard bounded triangular-array CLT and finite-multinomial information steps remain explicit compressions. EARLY KILL TEST: Run the draft's exact witness verifier, differentiate its recovery map on the 120-cell support face, and test positive coordinate variances plus singular-covariance max-quantile continuity; failure of rational ATT recovery or verbatim coverage by an existing theorem stops the run.
